source: a game that you can destroy buildings with natural disasters with super realistic graphics and super realistic physics and the city is massive

answers.ask: How massive is massive - a few dozen blocks, or a city you cannot cross on foot? It decides whether this is one map or several.
answers.answer: Make it one large continuous city map that takes a long time to cross on foot, with many dense blocks and varied building sizes.

answers.ask: Which disasters - earthquake, tornado, flood, meteor? Each one wants different terrain around the city.
answers.answer: Include earthquake, tornado, flood, and meteor disasters, all usable in the same city.

answers.ask: Is there scoring or an objective, or is destruction the whole point?
answers.answer: Destruction is the whole point; this should be a sandbox with no scoring or required objective.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: How massive is massive - a few dozen blocks, or a city you cannot cross on foot? It decides whether this is one map or several. A: Make it one large continuous city map that takes a long time to cross on foot, with many dense blocks and varied building sizes.
- [author] free — Q: Which disasters - earthquake, tornado, flood, meteor? Each one wants different terrain around the city. A: Include earthquake, tornado, flood, and meteor disasters, all usable in the same city.
- [author] goal — Q: Is there scoring or an objective, or is destruction the whole point? A: Destruction is the whole point; this should be a sandbox with no scoring or required objective.

## Enriched image prompt
Create one large continuous, densely built city that takes a long time to cross on foot. Lay out many connected urban blocks with varied building footprints and heights, broad streets between them, and enough open intersections for large-scale destruction to remain visible. Author every building as a highly realistic multi-part destructible structure with physically credible floors, walls, roofs, and structural sections. Keep the same city usable for earthquakes, tornadoes, floods, and meteor impacts: continuous low ground lets floodwater spread, streets provide tornado paths, and varied dense blocks provide clear collapse and impact targets. Use super-realistic materials, graphics, and physical construction throughout, with no scoring arena or objective destination.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation, specifically a physics sandbox. Causing disasters and observing realistic building destruction is the entire activity; survival and scoring are not requested.

## Shape and preset
Use `world-open`, called Shared Persistent World in this genre: one continuous city is available as a common destruction sandbox. Match the Physics Sim preset because physical reactions, breakable assemblies, dynamic hazards, and circulation through one shared space directly describe the request.

## Config requirements
Use `physics-rig` for buildings whose structural parts react credibly to forces and collapse. Use `destructible-cluster` from the shared catalogue for the authored multi-part building assemblies that earthquakes, tornadoes, floods, and meteors can break apart. Use `hazard-kill` for the visible disaster regions layered over the city. Use `path-circulation` for the connected street network between blocks and `settlement-density` for the many dense urban blocks.

## Layout requirements
No fixed post-segmentation placement is required. The earthquake, tornado, flood, and meteor systems are dynamic mechanics applied to the shared city rather than permanent trigger, spawn, pickup, or scoring volumes. Their implementation must use the destructible geometry already identified in the image configuration.

## Layout components
Build one continuous city containing many dense blocks, varied low-, mid-, and high-rise buildings, connected streets, broad intersections, and low ground over which floodwater can spread. Keep streets continuous across the map and distribute building sizes rather than concentrating all tall structures in one point. The city’s outer extent is the boundary. Compose enough of the map to communicate its scale while preserving individual structural assemblies as the key detail.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: realistic building construction and destruction-ready visual composition are authoritative, while no route or objective topology can make this sandbox unplayable.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use large scale, prioritizing legible buildings and structural detail across a dense city district while honouring the author’s one-map requirement. The theme is super-realistic contemporary urban destruction. Use `P0`: all geometry occupies one continuous city surface, and the requested physics and dynamic hazards do not themselves force an extra capture route.
